historical_references.reference: Gratiana was a name given to a few early Christian saints and martyrs. One of them was an unmarried virgin who was martyred during the reign of Emperor Diocletian in the late 3rd century. Her feast day is celebrated on May 12.

Another Gratiana, also an unmarried virgin, is believed to have lived in Rome in the 5th or 6th century. She was venerated as a saint and her relics were kept in the church of Santa Prassede. Her feast day is celebrated on October 14.
